definitions.explanation: A traditional celebration, often religious in origin, featuring ceremonies, processions, and entertainment.

examples.japanese: {夏|なつ}の{祭|まつ}りで{花火|はなび}を{見|み}た。
examples.english: I watched fireworks at the summer festival.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}で{祭|まつ}りが{行|おこな}われる。
examples.english: A festival is held at the shrine.

examples.japanese: {祭|まつ}りの{日|ひ}は{屋台|やたい}がたくさん{出|で}る。
examples.english: On festival days, many food stalls appear.

notes:
Can be written as {祭|まつり} or お{祭|まつ}り (polite form).

FAMOUS JAPANESE FESTIVALS:
・{祇園祭|ぎおんまつり} (Gion Festival - Kyoto)
・{天神祭|てんじんまつり} (Tenjin Festival - Osaka)
・{神田祭|かんだまつり} (Kanda Festival - Tokyo)
・{ねぶた祭|まつり} (Nebuta Festival - Aomori)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{祭|まつ}りに{行|い}く (to go to a festival)
・{祭|まつ}りを{楽|たの}しむ (to enjoy a festival)
・{夏祭|なつまつ}り (summer festival)
・{秋祭|あきまつ}り (autumn festival)
・{学園祭|がくえんさい} (school festival)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Many Japanese festivals (matsuri) have Shinto origins and involve carrying portable shrines ({神輿|みこし}) through the streets. Festival-goers often wear {浴衣|ゆかた}.
